Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of 1846000000.00 for the quarter ended July 31, 2026, which represents growth on a year earlier of 0.365385 according to the filing [D1]. The company delivered net income of 397000000.00 while non-GAAP net income was adjusted for items such as share-based compensation and acquisition costs as detailed in the release [D1]. Management stated that orders were up 56% on a reported basis with revenue of 1846000000.00 being up 36% on a reported basis during the period [D3]. The company ended the quarter with cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaling 2622000000.00 as shown in the financial statements [D1].

The Communications Solutions Group generated revenue of 1345000000.00 in the third quarter, up 43 percent from the prior year, reflecting 56 percent growth in commercial communications and 14 percent growth in aerospace, defense, and government [D1]. Within the division, wireline revenue surpassed wireless revenue for the first time this quarter as noted by management [D3]. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of 501000000.00 in the third quarter, up 21 percent from the prior year, reflecting growth across the semiconductor, general electronics and automotive and energy markets [D1]. Operating margin expanded by more than 800 basis points compared with the previous year as stated in the news report [D2].

Management forecast revenue of between 1930000000.00 and 1950000000.00 for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026 based on a weighted diluted share count of approximately 172 million shares [D1]. Non-GAAP earnings per share for the fourth fiscal quarter of 2026 are expected to be in the range of 3.34 to 3.40 as outlined in the results release [D1]. The substantial gap between Keysight's guidance and existing analyst forecasts provided investors with further evidence that strong demand could continue beyond the latest quarter according to the news report [D2]. Supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue as stated by the President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran in the earnings call summary [D3].

Analysts' tone was slightly negative to pressing on sustainability and constraints with repeated probing on demand durability and fulfillment including questions on whether demand is sustainable according to the sentiment analysis [D3]. Management's tone was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded in Q&A around constraints repeatedly returning to supply as a limiter as noted in the earnings call summary [D3]. The company repurchased approximately 640,000 shares of Keysight's stock at an average price of approximately 326 per share for a total consideration of 210 million during the quarter as stated by the Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty [D3].
